program.text: FROM ITEM_UNIT_OF_MEASURE itmUm RIGHT OUTER JOIN
STORAGE_TEMPLATE_DETAIL stDtl ON itmUm.QUANTITY_UM = stDtl.UNIT_OF_MEASURE AND ITEM =@Item AND (COMPANY=@Company OR COMPANY IS NULL)
(SELECT TOP 1 CASE WHEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE IS NOT NULL THEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE ELSE N'<literal:1>' END
FROM ITEM WHERE ITEM =@Item AND (COMPANY=@Company OR COMPANY IS NULL)) AND stDtl.UNIT_OF_MEASURE =@QuantityUM
FROM ITEM_UNIT_OF_MEASURE itmUm RIGHT OUTER JOIN
STORAGE_TEMPLATE_DETAIL stDtl ON itmUm.QUANTITY_UM = stDtl.UNIT_OF_MEASURE AND ITEM_CLASS=@ItemClass
(SELECT TOP 1 CASE WHEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE IS NOT NULL THEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE ELSE N'<literal:2>' END
FROM ITEM WHERE ITEM_CLASS=@ItemClass) AND stDtl.UNIT_OF_MEASURE =@QuantityUM
WHERE     ITEM = @Item AND (COMPANY=@Company OR COMPANY IS NULL)  AND QUANTITY_UM IN
(SELECT     TOP 1 CASE WHEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE IS NOT NULL THEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE ELSE N'<literal:3>' END
WHERE      ITEM = @Item AND (COMPANY=@Company OR COMPANY IS NULL)) AND SEQUENCE < @iSequence)
(SELECT     TOP 1 CASE WHEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE IS NOT NULL THEN STORAGE_TEMPLATE ELSE N'<literal:4>' END

reviewed_roles.purpose: Compute an insertion sequence from a storage-template unit sequence.

functional_roles.rationale: Compute an insertion sequence from a storage-template unit sequence. Item presence chooses item/company or item-class paths; unordered TOP 1 item template lookups and unordered variable assignment can select ambiguous candidates. A found sequence below one returns -1; otherwise return ISNULL(MAX(existing preceding unit sequence),0)+1. A NULL template sequence takes the ELSE path and returns 1 because the preceding comparison finds no rows. No unit row is inserted.

help_topics.title: Does a warehouse lookup change records?
help_topics.business_question: Does a warehouse lookup change records?
help_topics.plain_answer: Check the exact routine. Some calls only read data, while interface claim routines also change processing markers. For example, the transaction-history RU routine is read-only, the shipment RU routine marks a batch, and the accessorial-header lookup returns every header despite accepting an accessorial-code input.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify the captured routine and its actual body; prefixes are not proof of behavior.
Distinguish returned rows, output parameters and explicit RETURN values.
For interface claims, inspect the writes before treating the returned rows as a simple lookup.

configuration_dependencies: Processing conditions: claim ready or NULL rows as in process; output excludes processed rows. The leading unnamed value identifies an item-download record.

The output uses fixed receiving-interface-batch, new-action and processed-condition labels and a slash-separated tree path. The projected UTC stamp is rounded to seconds. These are returned interface labels, not writes to the source container rows.
The excluded IN_CONFIRMATION selector is affirmative. NULL load confirmation fails the inequality, and shipments lacking a matching shipping load fail the inner join.
The attribute selectors identify catch weight and its unit. TRY_CAST uses numeric(14,5); multiple values aggregate independently, and invalid weight text contributes NULL.

cases.question: Does wm_RUTransactionHistory01 update transaction history?
must_explain: No. It reads batch history and adds catch-weight information.
must_not_claim: RU always means an update.

cases.question: Does wm_RAccessorialHeader01 filter by its accessorial code parameter?
must_explain: No. The parameter is unused and all accessorial headers are selected.
must_not_claim: The input filters the rows.

cases.question: What does wm_RShipmentHeader03 return?
must_explain: An integer RETURN value: one when a matching header exists, otherwise zero; no rowset.
must_not_claim: It returns the complete shipment header.

help_topics.title: Why can a customer or vendor lookup return several matches?
help_topics.business_question: Why can a customer or vendor lookup return several matches?
help_topics.plain_answer: Several lookups include a company-specific record and a generic record whose company is blank in database terms (NULL). Most return all matches. Customer variant 04 alone limits the result to one, ranking specific ship-to and company combinations before generic combinations. Vendor and customer sort rules differ.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Check whether ship-to or ship-from must match exactly, may be NULL, or must be NULL on both sides.
Read the variant-specific ordering before interpreting the first row.
Treat tied preferred rows as unresolved unless another source establishes uniqueness.

cases.question: Does a customer company match always suppress generic customer rows?
must_explain: No. Several variants return both requested-company and NULL-company matches.
must_not_claim: Every routine returns a unique preferred record.

cases.question: How does customer lookup 04 choose a record?
must_explain: It limits to one and ranks both-specific, ship-to-specific, company-specific, then generic. Ties lack a further order.
must_not_claim: It sorts only alphabetically.

help_topics.title: How do item lookups handle company and cross-references?
help_topics.business_question: How do item lookups handle company and cross-references?
help_topics.plain_answer: Item lookups have different company rules. Some require exact company or both values NULL; others include generic items. Cross-reference joins can return the same item more than once. Item variant 03 does not prove that an item belongs to only one company; variant 11 separately counts all item rows.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify the exact item variant and company predicate.
Separate generic fallback from exact-or-both-NULL matching.
Check join multiplication and explicit uniqueness tests before assuming a single item.

configuration_dependencies: Company normalization uses one nonempty character as the NULL replacement. Two NULL values match, and NULL also matches that exact sentinel value; an empty string remains distinct.

cases.question: Does wm_RItem03 enforce one company for the item?
must_explain: No. It groups by company, so its per-company count does not enforce one company across the item.
must_not_claim: It proves company uniqueness.

cases.question: Can an item cross-reference lookup return duplicate item rows?
must_explain: Yes. Matching cross-reference joins can repeat ITEM rows because no DISTINCT is used.
must_not_claim: Each item is deduplicated automatically.

help_topics.title: How are item units and their sequence selected?
help_topics.business_question: How are item units and their sequence selected?
help_topics.plain_answer: Unit lookup 02 falls back by an entire set: exact item/company, then generic item, then item class. Other variants branch on whether an item was supplied. The sequence helper calculates a candidate number; the update helper shifts qualifying existing sequences. Neither helper creates the new unit row.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Distinguish set-level fallback from choosing a fallback separately for each unit.
Check whether a NULL item switches the lookup to item class.
Treat sequence calculation, shifting and insertion as separate steps with caller-owned coordination.

configuration_dependencies: The literals inside EXISTS projections are irrelevant to membership; those subqueries test row existence, not the projection value.

All four storage-template fallback literals name the default template; this fallback applies when the selected item's template is NULL. No matching item yields no template row instead of automatically creating a default item.

cases.question: Is item-unit fallback applied separately to each missing unit?
must_explain: No. Lookup 02 tests whether an item/company set exists before falling back.
must_not_claim: It fills every missing unit independently.

cases.question: Does the sequence helper insert the new unit?
must_explain: No. The read helper computes a sequence and the update helper shifts qualifying rows; insertion is separate.
must_not_claim: The helper completes unit creation.

help_topics.title: Why do operational and upload comments differ?
help_topics.business_question: Why do operational and upload comments differ?
help_topics.plain_answer: Comment routines can read operational comments or an upload copy depending on interface link. Their line rules differ: one treats line zero as including an operational NULL line, another uses ordinary equality, and a positive internal number can control whether an extra filter applies. The delete routine uses exact key equality.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify operational versus upload branch from the interface-link input.
Compare line-zero and NULL handling in the chosen routine.
Do not assume a displayed comment will match the delete predicate.

cases.question: Can line zero include comments with a NULL internal line?
must_explain: Yes in the operational branch of wm_RCommentText05; this is not universal across comment routines.
must_not_claim: All comment routines equate zero and NULL.

cases.question: Does a NULL line parameter delete a NULL-line comment?
must_explain: No. wm_DCommentText01 uses ordinary line equality.
must_not_claim: NULL equals NULL in its delete predicate.

help_topics.title: Which receipt and purchase-order records are selected?
help_topics.business_question: Which receipt and purchase-order records are selected?
help_topics.plain_answer: Business IDs are not the only scope. Some receipt and purchase-order lookups require warehouse and an open header, while others do not. A positive purchase-order line narrows one receipt-detail lookup; zero, negative or NULL line input selects all lines for that order. Projected columns also differ between variants.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Use the routine with the needed warehouse and open/closed restrictions.
Check whether company/type/ERP-order values use ordinary equality or explicit NULL normalization.
Check the output projection before treating joined receipt/header rows as detail-only data.

configuration_dependencies: ERP-order and receipt-type NULL normalization uses the same nonempty one-character sentinel within the applicable variants. NULLs match one another and can collide with a real sentinel value. ERP line uses ordinary equality; the warehouse-scoped variant also requires ordinary warehouse equality.

cases.question: Does wm_RReceiptHeader03 require an open receipt?
must_explain: No. It filters receipt ID and warehouse without testing CLOSE_DATE.
must_not_claim: Every receipt-header lookup excludes closed receipts.

cases.question: What does a zero line number mean to wm_RReceiptDetail05?
must_explain: It removes the purchase-order-line restriction and reads all lines for the order.
must_not_claim: It selects only line zero.

help_topics.title: How are receipt upload candidates chosen?
help_topics.business_question: How are receipt upload candidates chosen?
help_topics.plain_answer: The read-only candidate routines use container status, receipt closure and parent-container relationships. Variant 05 adds completed-detail checks. Variant 06 contains a comparison to NULL that does not act like an is-not-NULL test. A configuration branch can include closed unbatched receipts without qualifying containers; these reads do not claim a batch.
input_context: Use the exact routine variant and its parameter/NULL rules. No user-facing version/build choice is required.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify the candidate variant and status threshold.
Distinguish completed-detail, header-status and closed-receipt alternatives.
Keep candidate selection separate from batch marking and completed delivery.

configuration_dependencies: An interface configuration setting controls whether closed receipts without containers are included when its value is affirmative.
Variant 06 has ANSI_NULLS enabled, so CLOSE_DATE <> NULL does not identify a closed receipt.

cases.question: Does finding a receipt upload candidate mark it uploaded?
must_explain: No. These RReceiptHeader candidate routines only select headers.
must_not_claim: Selection assigns the upload batch.

cases.question: Does CLOSE_DATE <> NULL prove a receipt is closed in variant 06?
must_explain: No. Captured ANSI_NULLS is enabled and that comparison is UNKNOWN.
must_not_claim: It is equivalent to IS NOT NULL.

help_topics.title: What changes when receipt upload batches are selected?
help_topics.business_question: What changes when receipt upload batches are selected?
help_topics.plain_answer: The three receipt RU routines mark qualifying containers and headers with a batch, then return matching headers. They differ in completion and status conditions. Company and warehouse flags also differ: variant 03 lets the warehouse line-upload flag qualify a detail even when a company exists. Clearing a batch is a separate two-table update.

help_topics.plain_answer: Order claims can mark headers, details, containers, comments and VAS records, then return separate record sets. Claim stage order is order header, orphan detail, orphan container, orphan comment, orphan VAS. Each TOP subquery is ordered by INTERFACE_RECORD_ID and selects ready-or-NULL rows; only the header lacks orphan tests. The aggregate uses UNION of table counts, so equal count values deduplicate, but the final greater-than-zero test still expresses whether any included count is positive. The assigned condition denotes processed, while rows currently in process are excluded. NULL current condition is also excluded by inequality. This is not an in-process-to-processed transition.
The assigned condition denotes processed; every stamp-matching row in its four target tables is eligible.
